4218427430774c9c.title: Cialdin Tablet
4218427430774c9c.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for stomach pain, heartburn, food stagnation, and nausea.
4218427430774c9c.usage:
Adults aged 15 to under 80 years: take 2 tablets at a time. If needed, take 2 tablets at 4-hour intervals, up to 3 times daily. Do not exceed 3 times (6 tablets) per day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
4218427430774c9c.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to histamine H2-receptor antagonists; patients on dialysis; blood disorders; kidney or liver disease; stomach or duodenal disease; immune-system diseases such as asthma or rheumatism; a history of blood abnormalities such as decreased red blood cells, decreased platelets, or decreased white blood cells; pregnant or possibly pregnant women and breastfeeding women; children under 15 years and elderly aged 80 years or older; patients taking steroids, antibiotics, anticancer agents, or azole antifungals.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: elderly aged 65 years or older; a history of hypersensitivity to medicines; sore throat, cough, high fever, unexplained weight loss, or abdominal pain; a history of kidney disease. If symptoms do not improve after 3 days of use, stop taking and consult a pharmacist.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take together with steroids, antibiotics, anticancer agents, azole antifungals, or other stomach medicines. Consult a pharmacist before using together with bronchodilators (such as theophylline), anticoagulants (such as warfarin), antiepileptics (such as phenytoin), benzodiazepines (such as diazepam or triazolam), tricyclic antidepressants (such as imipramine), medicines for angina or high blood pressure (such as the beta-blocker propranolol), calcium antagonists (such as nifedipine), antiarrhythmics (such as mexiletine), macrolide antibiotics (such as tetracycline), new quinolone antibacterials (such as ofloxacin), or tetracycline antibiotics. Avoid alcoholic beverages while taking this medicine.

If severe symptoms appear over the skin, mouth, or eye mucous membranes throughout the body — such as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, and a high fever accompanied by rash, redness, and blistering edema — or if allergic symptoms (rash, flushing, itching, swelling), constipation, diarrhea, headache, fever, fatigue, weakness, cold-like symptoms, submucosal bleeding of the legs, numbness and stiffness of the limbs, palpitations, jaundice, generalized edema, or blood in the urine occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

ec46f83b056a84b9.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, promotion of digestion, upper abdominal bloating caused by indigestion, excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and sour belching.

ec46f83b056a84b9.caution:

0543e8bcca5c2663.title: Dazes Capsule
0543e8bcca5c2663.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, loss of appetite, overeating, food stagnation, promotion of digestion, and upper abdominal bloating caused by indigestion, and as adjunctive treatment for liver disease arising from insufficient bile secretion and for diseases of the biliary tract (bile ducts, gallbladder).
0543e8bcca5c2663.usage:
Adults: take 1 to 2 capsules, 3 times daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
0543e8bcca5c2663.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; acute hepatitis; severe biliary obstruction; radiolucent calcified gallstones; a non-functioning gallbladder; acute cholecystitis; pregnant or possibly pregnant women and breastfeeding women; children; kidney disease; peptic ulcer; inflammation of the large or small intestine such as Crohn's disease; hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: allergic constitution; severe pancreatic disease; gallstones; variceal bleeding; hepatic coma; ascites; conditions requiring liver transplantation; hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or a past reaction to it; elderly patients.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are taking other medicines.

If occasional diarrhea, loose stools, nausea, or vomiting; rarely abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn, or stomach discomfort; occasional itching; rarely rash, fever, cough, or interstitial pneumonia with abnormal chest X-ray; rarely general malaise, dizziness, mouth discomfort, calcification of gallstones, increased liver enzymes (ALT, ALP, AST, gamma-GT), or decreased white blood cells occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.
